resources.string: Tor stays connected while the VPN is off — turning it on takes under a second

• Tor keeps its bridge connection alive all the time — this uses battery, especially with Snowflake.\n• Your provider can see the bridge connection even while the VPN is off.\n• A permanent \"Tor on standby\" notification stays in the shade.
Tor starts connecting as soon as the app opens. If \"Connect\" is not tapped within a minute, it stops
About every 12 h on Wi-Fi or while charging: the next connection is faster
Less Tor overhead traffic (ReducedConnectionPadding). Slightly weaker protection against traffic analysis
Turn on \"Always-on VPN\" and \"Block connections without VPN\" in system settings: the tunnel starts by itself, and on failure no traffic bypasses Tor
The system may restrict the app — tap to lift it
Instructions for firmwares that close background apps
Status and speed in the notification
Turn Tor on and off from the shade
Add the \"Opal\" tile by hand: open the shade, tap \"Edit\" and drag the tile in
No glass refraction or background motion — lighter load and battery use. Turns on by itself in battery saver
A log for bug reports — only on request, editable before sending
Opal is distributed under the GNU GPL v3 or later. No telemetry, no analytics.

The exit country does not help against blocking — bridges do that. It only chooses which country websites see your traffic from. A narrow choice can slow the connection down; if the country has no suitable relays, Tor picks another.
You can choose a country after connecting: Tor learns relay countries from its database once online.
Recommended: Tor picks fast relays by itself
The log lives only in the memory of the tunnel process and contains no addresses or domains that apps connected to. Check and, if needed, edit the text before sending — it can only be sent by you.
The tunnel is not running — the log is empty. It appears after connecting.
Opal is built on free software. Tap a component to read its license.
Some firmwares close background apps even when they show a permanent notification. If the tunnel disappears by itself, allow Opal to run in the background:
Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO (MIUI / HyperOS): Settings → Apps → Opal → Autostart — on; Battery saver — \"No restrictions\".
Huawei (EMUI / HarmonyOS): Settings → Battery → App launch → Opal — \"Manage manually\", turn on all three switches.
Honor (MagicOS): Settings → Apps → App launch → Opal — \"Manage manually\", allow autostart and background activity.
Samsung (One UI): Settings → Battery → Background usage limits — remove Opal from \"Sleeping\" and \"Deep sleeping\" apps; set Opal to \"Unrestricted\".
OPPO, realme, OnePlus (ColorOS / OxygenOS): Settings → Battery → Opal — \"Allow background activity\"; in Apps → Opal — allow autostart.
vivo (OriginOS / Funtouch): i Manager → App management → Autostart → Opal — on; allow high background power use in battery settings.
Menu names depend on the firmware version. To check: turn the tunnel on, lock the screen for half an hour and see whether it is still connected.
